201	# Sprint 3: Project Development & Testing<a href="#sprint-3-project-development-testing" class="headerlink"
202	title="Permanent link">¶</a>
203	
204	**Nov 3 – Nov 19 · All deliverables due Nov 19, 11:59 PM (mid-sprint
205	check-in due Nov 12) · 100 points (12% of course grade)**
206	
207	Sprint 3 continues the development of your project and puts the focus on
208	**testing**: how well your tests check what your code is supposed to do.
209	The issue backlog, PR workflow, and general expectations carry forward;
210	see [Sprint 1](../sprint1/) and [Sprint 2](../sprint2/) for anything not
211	explicitly changed here. This page covers what is **new or different**
212	in Sprint 3.
213	
214	------------------------------------------------------------------------
215	
216	<div class="admonition abstract">
217	
218	Sprint 3 at a glance
219	
220	**Key dates:** Nov 12: check-in + at least one code PR (open or merged)
221	· Nov 19: everything else
222	
223	**Important rules (they cost the most points):**
224	
225	- No merge without an approval on the latest commit.
226	- Spec review on the issue, saying what was checked.
227	- Every code PR links its issue.
228	- Real AI logs.
229	- Test Evidence table in every PR; expected values not copied from the
230	  code's output.
231	- Mutation testing with a tool, before and after reports committed.
232	- Your team introduces no new test failures; skipped tests and disabled
233	  checks need an issue.
234	
235	</div>
236	
237	<div class="admonition tip">
238	
239	Unfamiliar with a term?
240	
241	Check the [Glossary](../glossary/) for definitions of terms used
242	throughout this page.
243	
244	</div>
245	
246	------------------------------------------------------------------------
247	
248	### Before you begin<a href="#before-you-begin" class="headerlink"
249	title="Permanent link">¶</a>
250	
251	- **Check your AI log setup** against the [AI Log
252	  Instructions](../ai-logs/) before your first session.
253	- **Read "Things that must improve"** below. These issues were observed
254	  in Sprint 2 and will be graded strictly.
255	- **Record your baseline early** (see D8): the test results at your
256	  Sprint 2 release tag (`-csci435-s2`), from CI or by running the
257	  relevant test suites locally. It helps you find hardening issues and
258	  get the mutation tool running.
259	- **Try the mutation testing tool early** (see D6), on any existing file
260	  in the part of the code you work on. Do not wait until your PRs are
261	  ready.
262	
263	------------------------------------------------------------------------
264	
265	### What is new in Sprint 3<a href="#what-is-new-in-sprint-3" class="headerlink"
266	title="Permanent link">¶</a>
267	
268	- **Mutation testing** (D6): a new individual deliverable. It
269	  **replaces** the UML diagrams from Sprint 2.
270	- **Test evidence section** in every PR description (D4).
271	- **Hardening issues**: one of your issues may be a hardening issue
272	  (D1).
273	- **Suite health section** in the sprint report (D8).
274	- **Mid-sprint check-in requires an open PR** (D7), due Nov 12.
275	
276	<div class="admonition info">
277	
278	Team feature for Sprints 3–4
279	
280	Each team will be assigned a larger feature that spans Sprints 3 and 4.
281	The instructor or TA will post it as an issue in your team's issue
282	tracker and notify your team when it is posted. You will likely need to
283	split it into sub-issues.
284	
285	</div>
286	
287	------------------------------------------------------------------------
288	
289	### Things that must improve from Sprint 2<a href="#things-that-must-improve-from-sprint-2" class="headerlink"
290	title="Permanent link">¶</a>
291	
292	These issues were observed in Sprint 2 and will be graded strictly in
293	Sprint 3.
294	
295	**1. Open PRs early.** In Sprint 2, most PRs were opened in the last two
296	days, which left no time for review. In Sprint 3, you need a code PR by
297	the mid-sprint check-in (see D7).
298	
299	**2. Independent approval before merging.** A PR is merged only after a
300	teammate approves its **latest commit**. Merging without an approval, or
301	after pushing new commits since the approval, is not allowed. Once
302	approved, the author may merge. To keep reviews moving, request the
303	review on GitHub and notify your reviewer on Zulip; reviewers respond
304	(approve or request changes) within 24 hours.
305	
306	**3. Spec reviews must be visible and show what was checked.** Before
307	coding starts, a teammate posts a review comment on the issue itself.
308	The comment states what the reviewer checked: whether each acceptance
309	criterion is clear and testable, which cases were considered (and
310	whether they are covered), and whether the scope fits. If the reviewer
311	finds problems, they list them and the author updates the spec. If the
312	spec is good, the reviewer says so and approves, but "Looks good!" with
313	nothing about what was checked is not acceptable.
314	
315	**4. Link PRs and issues.** Every code PR must link the issue it
316	addresses, so the PR can be checked against the spec. Use
317	`Closes #<issue>` in the PR description so the issue closes
318	automatically when the PR is merged, and attach issues and code PRs to
319	the `Sprint 3` milestone.
320	
321	**5. AI logs must be real logs.** A log shows your prompts and the AI's
322	output (SpecStory format recommended; see the [AI Log
323	Instructions](../ai-logs/)). The following are **not** logs and receive
324	no full credit: summaries of a session, paraphrased prompts, a share
325	link to a chat, or tool output without the prompts that produced it.
326	File names must follow `YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`. Link the log
327	from the issue or PR it documents.
328	
329	**6. The sprint report must render.** Check that tables and links
330	display correctly on GitHub (no escaped `\|` or `\[`). Use the Sprint 3
331	sections, not a copy of a previous report.
332	
333	------------------------------------------------------------------------
334	
335	### Deliverables<a href="#deliverables" class="headerlink" title="Permanent link">¶</a>
336	
337	#### D1 - Sprint Backlog<a href="#d1-sprint-backlog" class="headerlink"
338	title="Permanent link">¶</a>
339	
340	Same process as Sprint 2 ([D1](../sprint2/#d1-sprint-backlog)),
341	including the priority on carryovers: unfinished Sprint 2 issues go into
342	your Sprint 3 backlog first, or you document on the issue why they are
343	dropped.
344	
345	**Scope minimums for Sprint 3** (same as Sprint 2):
346	
347	| Role | Minimum issues |
348	|----|----|
349	| Each CSCI 435 member | at least 2 medium issues (or equivalent story points) |
350	| Each CSCI 535 (grad) member | at least 2 medium issues + 1 additional small issue (or equivalent story points) |
351	
352	**Scope must be justified.** Each issue states its scope (small or
353	medium) and one or two sentences on why: which components it touches and
354	how much change you expect. The instructor or TA may reclassify an issue
355	whose scope is clearly overstated.
356	
357	**Hardening issues (optional).** One of your issues may be a *hardening
358	issue*: work that makes the existing system more reliable rather than
359	adding a feature. Good sources:
360	
361	- **Your baseline run** (see D8): failing tests, flaky tests, or broken
362	  CI checks on `main`.
363	- **Tech debt your team recorded** in the "Introduced" and "Encountered"
364	  fields of your Sprint 1 and Sprint 2 PRs.
365	- **Known bugs** found in reviews, after merging, or by teammates.
366	- **The upstream issue tracker**, for bugs in the parts of the system
367	  your team works on.
368	
369	A hardening issue is scoped like any other issue (see the scope
370	justification above). It must also include evidence that the problem is
371	fixed:
372	
373	- **Bug fix:** a test that fails before the fix and passes after.
374	- **Flaky test:** the root cause, and enough repeated runs of that test
375	  before and after the fix to show the change (for example, 20 runs for
376	  a unit test or 10 for an E2E test).
377	- **Broken or missing CI check:** links to CI runs before and after the
378	  fix.
379	- **Failing tests in the baseline:** pass/fail counts before and after,
380	  and the cause of each group of failures.
381	
382	Regenerating snapshots, reformatting code, or silencing a check without
383	fixing its cause counts as small at most.

437	    |---|---|---|---|

452	- **Test(s):** the test name (and file, if not obvious). If you checked

457	- **Source of expected value:** where the expected result in your test
458	  comes from. Use one of: `AC`, `issue discussion`, `docs`,
459	  `upstream behavior`, or `other` (explain). **The current output of
460	  your own code is not a valid source**; a test whose expected value was
461	  copied from what the code returns cannot detect that the code is
462	  wrong.
463	- **Not tested automatically, and why:** only for ACs checked manually
464	  only.
465	- You may use AI to draft this section, but you are responsible for
466	  checking that it is accurate.
467	
468	Example:
469	
470	| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level | Source of expected value |
471	|----|----|----|----|

474	| AC3: The badge text is readable in dark mode | Manual: enabled dark mode, opened the booking page during the window → badge text is readable | manual | issue discussion |

476	**Not tested automatically, and why:** AC3 depends on visual contrast,
477	which our test setup does not check.

502	#### D6 - Mutation Testing *(new)*<a href="#d6-mutation-testing-new" class="headerlink"
503	title="Permanent link">¶</a>
504	
505	This is a new individual deliverable.
506	
507	**What it is.** A mutation testing tool makes small changes to your code
508	(*mutants*), such as flipping a condition or changing a boundary value,
509	and runs your tests against each one. If a test fails, the mutant is
510	*killed*. If all tests pass, the mutant *survived*: your tests did not
511	notice that the code changed. Survivors point to weak or missing tests.
512	
513	**What to do.** For **one of your issues whose PR changes source code
514	and tests** (CSCI 535: **two** such issues; your small issue may be one
515	of them):
516	
517	1.  Run a mutation testing tool on the **source files changed by your
518	    PR(s)** for that issue. Do not run it on the whole project.
519	2.  Using the tool's report, analyze every surviving mutant: is it
520	    *equivalent* (it behaves exactly like the original code, so no test
521	    can kill it), or does it reveal a gap in your tests? If there are
522	    more than 10 surviving mutants, analyze at least 10, starting with
523	    those in lines your PR added or changed.
524	3.  Add or strengthen **at least one test that kills a surviving
525	    mutant** that revealed a gap. Re-run the tool to confirm it is
526	    killed. If no surviving mutant reveals a gap (all are killed or
527	    equivalent), say so and justify it in the surviving-mutants table;
528	    that completes this step.
529	4.  **Answer the questions in the template below**.
530	
531	**Evidence.** Configure the tool to write a machine-readable report
532	(StrykerJS: add `"json"` to `reporters`; Gremlins:
533	`--output=<file>.json`; go-mutesting: save the terminal output to a text
534	file). Commit the report from your first run and from your re-run as
535	`docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json` and
536	`-after.json` (`.txt` for go-mutesting). The mutation scores you list
537	must match the reports, and the mutant your new test kills must show as
538	killed in the "after" report.
539	
540	**A tool is required.** Manual mutation does not count.
541	
542	| Stack | Tool |
543	|----|----|
544	| TypeScript/JavaScript with Vitest (Actual Budget, Cal.diy, Excalidraw, Outline, Gitea frontend) | [StrykerJS](https://stryker-mutator.io/) with the [Vitest runner](https://stryker-mutator.io/docs/stryker-js/vitest-runner/) |
545	| TypeScript/JavaScript with Jest (Medusa) | [StrykerJS](https://stryker-mutator.io/) with the [Jest runner](https://stryker-mutator.io/docs/stryker-js/jest-runner/) |
546	| Go (Gitea backend) | [Gremlins](https://gremlins.dev/) or [go-mutesting](https://github.com/avito-tech/go-mutesting) |
547	
548	**Set it up early.** Getting the tool to work on a large codebase is
549	real work: builds, services, and choosing which tests run. Each student
550	configures and runs the tool for their own files and commits the
551	configuration they used. You may reuse a teammate's setup (and are
552	encouraged to), as long as you run the tool yourself and credit the
553	teammate in your report.
554	
555	**Common problems** to watch for:
556	
557	- **The tool stops before mutating.** Tools first run your tests on the
558	  unchanged code. If any of the selected tests fail, the run stops. Fix
559	  or exclude failing tests first (this is where your baseline run
560	  helps).
561	- **Tests run against built code.** If your tests run against compiled
562	  output (for example, a `dist` folder) instead of the source, mutants
563	  in the source are never seen by the tests. Configure the tool to
564	  rebuild before testing, or choose tests that run on source.
565	- **Tests need services.** Some test suites need a database or another
566	  service running. Start them before running the tool.
567	- **False survivors.** If you limit which tests run (for example, with
568	  Vitest's `dir` option), make sure the tests that cover the mutated
569	  files are included. Otherwise, mutants that some test would catch are
570	  reported as survived or not covered. Before writing a new test for a
571	  survivor, check that the relevant tests actually ran.
572	- **Long runs.** Mutating only the files changed by your PR keeps run
573	  time manageable.
574	
575	<div class="admonition warning">
576	
577	If you are blocked
578	
579	If you cannot get the tool to run, first ask your teammates: someone may
580	already have a working setup. If you are still stuck, tell the TA **as
581	early as possible**, with the errors you got and the AI log of what you
582	tried. The TA will help you debug it. If it still cannot be made to
583	work, the TA may approve running the tool on a different issue or a
584	different part of your code instead. Problems reported at the end of the
585	sprint will not excuse a missing D6.
586	
587	</div>
588	
589	**Submission:** `docs/sprint3/mutation/<issue#>-<username>.md`, using
590	this template:
591	
592	<div class="highlight">
593	
594	    # Mutation testing: Issue #<N> -- <issue title>
595	
596	    **PR(s):** #...  **Tool:** ...  **Config:** [link; credit the teammate if you reused their setup]  **Command:** `...`
597	    **Reports:** [before](reports/<issue#>-<username>-before.json) · [after](reports/<issue#>-<username>-after.json)
598	    **Mutation score:** before ...% → after ...%
599	
600	    ## Surviving mutants
601	
602	    | Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |
603	    |---|---|---|---|
604	    | | | | |
605	
606	    ## New or strengthened test
607	
608	    Commit: [link] · Test: [file › test name] · Kills: [mutant location]
609	
610	    ## Questions
611	
612	    1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?
613	    2. Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain.
614	    3. If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and what did you verify or correct? If AI was not used, write "N/A."
615	
616	</div>

59	- **Reviews:** nobody approves or merges their own PR. Reviewers leave substantive comments, not a
60	  bare approval. Tell the reviewer on Zulip or by email, and aim to review within 24 hours. Each
61	  student reviews at least one PR per sprint, and every teammate at least once per semester.
62	- **Extra credit:** up to 3 points per PR submitted to upstream Gitea that is accepted or under
63	  active review, at the instructor's discretion.
64	
65	## Branches and commits
66	
67	- Branches: `feat/issue-<N>-short-description`, `fix/issue-<N>-short-description` or
68	  `chore/short-description` (`STUDENTS.md`). One issue per branch.
69	- Commit messages follow Conventional Commits and end with the issue number:
70	  `feat(repo): show empty state on releases page (#17)`. Add an
71	  `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer when AI helped; never `Co-Authored-By` or
72	  `Signed-off-by` (`AGENTS.md`). A human approves every commit before it is made.
73	
74	### Before each implementation: sync with main
75	
76	Every new branch starts from an up-to-date `main`. AI sessions run this before writing any code:
77	
78	```bash
79	git switch main
80	git pull origin main
81	git switch -c feat/issue-<N>-short-description
82	```
83	
84	To pick up new work on `main` for a branch that already exists, **merge, don't rebase**. Rebasing
85	or squashing after review has started is not allowed (`docs/sprint0/standards.md`):
86	
87	```bash
88	git fetch origin
89	git merge origin/main
90	```
91	
92	Do this before opening the PR and again if `main` moves while it is in review. Never merge another
93	feature branch into yours.
94	
95	### After merge: clean up
96	
97	A PR is merged with a merge commit once it is approved, every review comment is addressed and CI
98	passes. Then:
99	
100	```bash
101	git switch main
102	git pull origin main
103	git branch -d feat/issue-<N>-short-description               # local branch
104	git push origin --delete feat/issue-<N>-short-description    # or GitHub's "Delete branch" button
105	git fetch --prune                                            # drop stale remote-tracking refs
106	```
107	
108	Also check that the issue closed (via `Closes #N`), is on the sprint milestone, and has its AI
109	Assistance comment. Then run `specstory sync` and file the session's log (see `ai-logs/README.md`).
110	
111	## Issue format: feature (user story)
112	
113	Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/user-story.yaml`. The user story must meet INVEST: Independent,
114	Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable.
115	
116	```markdown
117	## User Story
118	As a <role>, I want <capability> so that <benefit>.
119	
120	## User Scenario
121	<A short concrete walk-through: who, where in the UI, what they do, what they see.>
122	
123	## Acceptance Criteria
124	- [ ] AC1: Given <state>, when <action>, then <observable result>.
125	- [ ] AC2: ...
126	- [ ] AC3: ...            (at least 3; each has a clear pass/fail result)
127	
128	## Out of Scope
129	- <What this issue deliberately does not do.>
130	
131	## Open Questions
132	- <Unresolved questions, or "None".>
133	
134	## Design Decision
135	**Decision:** <what was chosen>
136	**Alternatives Considered:** <at least two concrete options, and why each lost>
137	**Rationale:** <why this one>
138	**Consequences:** <trade-offs, follow-up work, what it makes harder>
139	
140	## Scope
141	small | medium | large, and matching `scope:` label
142	```
143	
144	## Issue format: bug report
145	
146	Template: `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug-report.yaml`.
147	
148	```markdown
149	## Observed Behavior
150	## Expected Behavior
151	## Steps to Reproduce
152	1. ...
153	## Additional Information
154	<Version or commit, browser/OS, logs, screenshots.>
155	## Design Decision
156	<Same four fields as above: Decision, Alternatives Considered, Rationale, Consequences.>
157	```
158	
159	- **Design Decision (D3):** fill it in once you've picked an approach, before opening the PR. Put
160	  a second decision under another `### Decision 2` heading. If a PR changes the decision, update
161	  the issue body.
162	- **Peer review (D2):** a teammate reads the spec and comments `Spec reviewed — <notes>` on the
163	  issue before implementation starts.
164	
165	## Pull request format
166	
167	Template: `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Title uses Conventional Commits, e.g.
168	`fix(issues): keep label filter after search`. Description sections:
169	
170	1. `Closes #<N>`, which links the issue and closes it on merge.
171	2. **What changed:** the change in your own words.
172	3. **Why:** the problem, and which acceptance criteria (AC1…) it satisfies.
173	4. **How it was tested / Test strategy:** tests added or updated and why these ones. Name any
174	   change that can't be tested automatically and how it was checked by hand. Every behaviour change
175	   needs a new or updated test.
176	5. **CI / manual verification:** CI status, or the commands run and their results.
177	6. **Design:** one line pointing at the Design Decision in the issue, or a note on how it changed.
178	7. **Tech Debt:** required from Sprint 2. Both fields are required, and `None.` is a valid answer:
179	
180	   ```markdown
181	   ## Tech Debt
182	
183	   **Introduced:** <shortcuts, workarounds or design compromises this PR makes, and why>
184	
185	   **Encountered:** <tech debt that was already there and that you ran into, and how you handled it>
186	   ```
187	
188	8. **AI assistance:** format in `AI-ASSISTANCE.md` §2, with **no log link**.
189	
190	Per-PR grading (20 points): correctness against the acceptance criteria 6, test strategy with
191	explanation 5, description quality including the Tech Debt section 4, CI or manual verification 3,
192	review rubric posted 2.
193	
194	## Code review rubric
195	
196	The reviewer posts this as a **PR comment**, as well as the GitHub review itself. A copy-paste copy
197	is in `.github/code-review-rubric.md`, so keep the two in sync. Pull the branch and test it when you
198	can, say what you checked, and mark each point as required or optional
199	(`docs/community-governance.md`). Score each row against the issue's acceptance criteria. Anything
200	below 7 needs a note saying what would raise it.
201	
202	```markdown
203	### Code Review — @reviewer-username
204	
205	**Checked:** <what you ran or tried>
206	
207	| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
208	| --- | --- | --- |
209	| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
210	| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
211	| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
212	| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
213	| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
214	| Overall — merge as-is? | | |
215	```
216	
217	## UML diagrams (D6)
218	
219	The person who resolved a medium issue draws a class diagram and a sequence diagram for it. Several
220	small issues that together equal one medium issue are drawn together instead. Files:
221	
222	- `docs/sprint2/diagrams/<issue#>-<github-username>-class.png` (or `.pdf`)
223	- `docs/sprint2/diagrams/<issue#>-<github-username>-sequence.png` (or `.pdf`)
224	- `docs/sprint2/diagrams/<issue#>-<github-username>.md`, which embeds both and answers the Q&A
225	
226	What the diagrams need:
227	
228	- Show the existing code found during concept location and impact analysis, and the new or changed
229	  code, and tell the two apart with a legend, colour or label.
230	- Show only the fields and methods that matter to the issue.
231	- Annotate the diagrams with the key design decisions and calls. Diagrams without annotations lose
232	  points.
233	- Add a short note on how Go maps to UML: structs, interfaces, and embedding.
234	- The `.md` follows the course template: `# Issue #<N> -- <title>`, `## Class Diagram`,
235	  `## Sequence Diagram`, `## Q&A`, each diagram embedded with
236	  `![Class diagram](<issue#>-<github-username>-class.png)` under its heading. The Q&A has 3
237	  class-diagram questions, 3 sequence-diagram questions and 1 question on AI use, answered "N/A" if
238	  no AI was used. The questions, copied from the Sprint 2 page:
239	
240	```markdown
241	**Class diagram:**
242	
243	1. Among all the classes shown in the diagram, which 1--2 are most central to understanding the codebase and solving the issue? Explain what role each one plays.
244	2. What is the most significant relationship shown in the diagram? Explain what it represents in the system and why it matters for understanding the solution.
245	3. Looking back at your implementation, is there anything in this design you would change, and why?
246	
247	**Sequence diagram:**
248	
249	1. What user action or system event starts the sequence, and what is the expected outcome when it completes successfully?
250	2. Identify the 2--3 most important steps in the sequence. For each one, describe what is happening and note whether it involves existing code or new/modified code from your solution.
251	3. What error cases or alternative paths are not shown in the diagram, and why did you leave them out?
252	
253	**Cross-cutting:**
254	
255	4. If you used AI to create or check any part of the diagrams, describe what it produced, what you verified against the actual code, and what you had to correct or add. If AI was not used, write "N/A."
256	```
257	
258	Grading (15 points): existing code 2, solution code 2, annotations 3, UML notation (relationships,
259	cardinality, lifelines; minor errors are fine) 2, Q&A 4, AI transparency 2. The Q&A points are for
260	understanding that goes beyond what the diagram already shows, so answer with reasons, not a
261	re-description of the boxes.
262	
263	## Sprint report (D8) sections
264

266	
267	- Team: names, GitHub usernames, project name, repository link.

273	- Test strategy, including untestable changes and why.

276	- Release: tag and release link.
277	- Risks and retrospective: what worked, what slowed the team down, next-sprint changes.

279	- From Sprint 2: Sprint 1 carryovers (which were taken, which were skipped and why), and D6 and D7

# .claude-students — start here

Course-only documentation for the CSCI-435 Gitea fork. It exists so a person — or an AI session —
can read one or two short pages instead of exploring ~150 Go packages. That exploration is the
single largest avoidable cost on this project, in your time and in tokens.

This page is the quick start: what is here, what tools you have, and the three things you will
actually need to do.

## Two layers, same content

| | `docs/` | `guide/` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Written for | an AI session | a person |
| Style | terse, every claim cites a file | explains, defines jargon, names symptoms |
| Length | ~80 lines | up to 200 |
| Status | **the source of truth** | a rendering of it |

Both have the same 34 filenames, so `guide/models-db.md` explains `docs/models-db.md`.

**`guide/` is derived from `docs/`.** Each guide stores a fingerprint of its source page, so if the
reference changes and the guide is not regenerated, the validator says so. **If the two ever
disagree, the guide is wrong** — fix the reference page, not the guide.

## What is in this folder

| File | What it is for |
| --- | --- |
| `INDEX.md` | Routing table: "working on X → read Y". Loaded into every AI session. |
| `guide/START-HERE.md` | **If you are new to this codebase, read this first.** |
| `guide/*.md` | A plain-English page per reference page. |
| `docs/*.md` | The reference pages. Terse, citation-heavy. |
| `MAINTENANCE.md` | The 22 rules. Read before editing anything here. |
| `_TEMPLATE.md`, `guide/_TEMPLATE.md` | The only permitted shapes for a new page. |
| `check.sh` | The validator. Run it before you push. |

## Your toolkit

One command:

```sh
./.claude-students/check.sh
```

It prints `check.sh: ok (34 docs, guide 34/34)` when everything is fine, or `file: message (rule N)`
for each problem. It is dependency-free and finishes in under a second.

It checks, among other things: that every page follows its template, stays under its line cap, cites
only paths that exist, and is listed in `INDEX.md`; that no two reference pages claim the same code;
that **every guide matches the fingerprint of its source page**; and that a guide cites no path its
source page does not — so a guide can add explanation, but never new facts.

## The three things you will actually do

### 1. You are new and want to understand the codebase

Read `guide/START-HERE.md`, then `guide/architecture.md`, then `guide/testing.md`. After that, read
only the page for whatever you are touching. Do not read all 34.

`INDEX.md` maps tasks to pages.

### 2. You found a page that is wrong or incomplete

This is expected, and fixing it is part of the work — not a favour.

1. Fix **`docs/<name>.md`**, never the guide. Every claim needs a repo path; no line numbers, only
   file plus symbol name.
2. Regenerate **`guide/<name>.md`** to match, and update its `source-hash` to the first 16
   characters of `sha256sum .claude-students/docs/<name>.md`.
3. Run `./.claude-students/check.sh`.
4. Ship both in the same pull request as the code change that taught you this, titled
   `docs(context): <subject>`.

If you skip step 2 the validator will tell you, by name, on the next run.

The easiest way to do step 2 is to ask an AI session: *"`docs/<name>.md` changed — regenerate
`guide/<name>.md` from it and update the hash."*

### 3. You are starting a fresh AI session

You do not have to do anything. `CLAUDE.md` imports `INDEX.md`, so every Claude session already has
the routing table, and `AGENTS.md` points other tools at it.

If a session starts exploring the tree instead of reading a page, say: *"Read
`.claude-students/INDEX.md` and use the page for this area."*

If you ask a session to change documentation here, point it at `MAINTENANCE.md` — rules 16-22 are
the ones about keeping the two layers in step.

## Not upstream

This folder is **ours**, not Gitea's, and is deliberately self-contained so it can be removed in one
step if this fork is ever merged upstream:

```sh
rm -rf .claude-students/
```

Then remove the two pointers: the `@.claude-students/INDEX.md` line in `CLAUDE.md`, and the
`.claude-students/INDEX.md` bullet in `AGENTS.md`. Nothing else refers to this folder — no
`Makefile` target, no CI job.

## Authority

These pages never override the project's own rules. `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and
`docs/guidelines-*.md` at the repository root are authoritative; the pages here summarise them and
point at code. If a page here contradicts one of those, the page here is wrong.

Note that `docs/` means two different things depending on where you are standing: inside this
folder it is our reference pages, at the repository root it is Gitea's own documentation. The guides
say "in this folder" or "Gitea's own" wherever it could be ambiguous.
<!-- markdownlint-disable MD029 -->
<!-- Rules are numbered continuously 1-15 across the sections below; check.sh error
     messages and all 34 docs cite them by number, so the sequence must not restart. -->

# Maintenance rules

Five people maintain one shared set of docs. These rules exist so the set stays *one* set. Read
them before editing anything in `.claude-students/`. Rules marked **[checked]** are enforced by
`./.claude-students/check.sh`.

## Scope discipline

1. **Upstream wins.** `AGENTS.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/guidelines-*.md` are authoritative.
   Docs here summarise them and link to them; they never restate a rule differently and never
   contradict one. A contradiction is a bug in this folder, not in the project.
2. **One fact, one home.** Every fact lives in exactly one doc — the one whose `scope:` owns that
   path. Everywhere else, link to it. Duplicated facts are how five maintainers end up with five
   different answers.
3. **Durability test.** Record a fact only if it (a) took more than one discovery step to find and
   (b) will still be true after the next upstream merge. A one-off workaround, a sprint detail or
   anything about your own task fails this test — that belongs in `ai-logs/`.
4. **No process notes.** No TODOs, no open questions, no first person, no student names, no dates
   other than `verified-at`. This is a map of the code, not a journal.

## Form

5. **Template only [checked].** Use the `## ` headings from `_TEMPLATE.md`, all of them, in that
   order, with nothing added. If a section has nothing to say, write one line saying so.
6. **120-line cap [checked].** Going over means the scope is too broad. Split the doc, and add the
   new `INDEX.md` row in the same commit. `INDEX.md` itself is capped at 60 lines.
7. **Cite or delete [checked, partially].** Every claim names a repo path. A claim with no path is
   unverifiable by the next reader — delete it.
8. **Symbols, not line numbers [checked].** Write `models/db/context.go` → `WithTx`, never
   `models/db/context.go:143`. Line numbers rot at the next upstream merge and a stale number is
   worse than no number. Code fences stay at 10 lines or fewer — point at the file instead of
   copying it.
9. **Repo-relative paths [checked].** `models/db/context.go`, never `/home/you/gitea/models/...`.
10. **Whitespace [checked].** No trailing whitespace, LF endings, final newline — same as the rest
    of the repo (`.editorconfig`).

## Change control

11. **One universal set.** These docs live on `main` and nowhere else. Never keep a personal copy,
    a per-student folder, or a long-lived branch of them.
12. **Changes land by PR**, titled `docs(context): <subject>` per `AGENTS.md` Conventional Commits,
    with an `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer and no `Co-Authored-By` or
    `Signed-off-by`.
13. **Fix in place.** If you discover while working that a doc is wrong or incomplete, correct it
    in the *same* PR as your code change and update `verified-at` to the commit you checked
    against. Leaving a doc stale for someone else to hit is the exact failure this folder exists to
    prevent. This rule applies to AI sessions too.
14. **New docs need three things in one commit [checked]:** the file, its `INDEX.md` row, and a
    `scope:` that does not overlap any existing doc's. If the scope overlaps, you wanted to edit
    that doc, not add one.
15. **`./.claude-students/check.sh` passes before you push [checked].** It is dependency-free and
    finishes in under a second.

## The guide layer (rules 16-22)

`guide/` holds a plain-English page for each reference page in `docs/`, same filename. It exists so
a person new to Go and to this codebase can get oriented. It is **derived**, not independent.

16. Every guide carries `source:`, `source-hash:` and `verified-at:` in its frontmatter **[checked]**.
17. A guide's `source:` names a real `docs/*.md` with the **same filename** **[checked]**.
18. `source-hash:` is the first 16 characters of `sha256sum docs/<name>.md`. If the reference page
    changes and the guide is not regenerated, `check.sh` reports **drift** **[checked]**. Regenerating
    means: reread the reference page, rewrite the guide, update the hash and `verified-at`.
19. Guide headings match `guide/_TEMPLATE.md` exactly and in order **[checked]**.
20. Guides are capped at **200 lines**, code fences at **30** **[checked]** — teaching needs more room
    than reference does.
21. **A guide adds explanation, vocabulary and worked steps. It adds no new facts.** Every repo path
    a guide cites must also be cited by its source page **[checked]**. If you need a fact the
    reference page lacks, add it *there* first, which bumps the hash and forces the guide to be
    regenerated in the same commit — exactly the intended order.
22. `guide/START-HERE.md` has no source page. It is exempt from rules 17, 18 and 21, and is where
    cross-cutting material lives that no single reference page owns.

**Never fix a fact in `guide/`.** If the two layers disagree, the reference page is the truth and
the guide is stale: fix `docs/`, regenerate the guide, ship both in one PR. A disagreement is a bug
report against `docs/`, not an editing job in `guide/`.

**Known limitation:** a hand-edit to a guide that only rewords prose is not mechanically
detectable. Rule 21 catches invented facts; rule 18 catches a stale guide; review catches the rest.

## Updating `verified-at`

`verified-at` is the short SHA the doc was last checked against, from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`.
Bump it whenever you confirm or correct a doc. A doc whose `verified-at` is far behind `main` has
not been checked recently — treat its details as hints and confirm them in the code before relying
on them.
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Validates .claude-students against the mechanical rules in MAINTENANCE.md.
# Dependency-free. Run from anywhere: ./.claude-students/check.sh
set -uo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 1

DIR=".claude-students"
TEMPLATE="$DIR/_TEMPLATE.md"
INDEX="$DIR/INDEX.md"
MAX_LINES=120
MAX_INDEX_LINES=60
MAX_FENCE=10

fail=0
err() {
  printf '%s: %s\n' "$1" "$2" >&2
  fail=1
}

for required in "$TEMPLATE" "$INDEX" "$DIR/MAINTENANCE.md" "$DIR/README.md"; do
  [ -f "$required" ] || err "$required" "missing"
done
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1

check_whitespace() {
  local file="$1" line
  line=$(grep -n '[[:space:]]$' "$file" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  [ -z "$line" ] || err "$file:$line" "trailing whitespace (rule 10)"
  [ -z "$(tail -c 1 "$file")" ] || err "$file" "no final newline (rule 10)"
}

for meta in "$TEMPLATE" "$INDEX" "$DIR/MAINTENANCE.md" "$DIR/README.md"; do
  check_whitespace "$meta"
done

want_h2=$(grep '^## ' "$TEMPLATE")

index_lines=$(wc -l < "$INDEX")
if [ "$index_lines" -gt "$MAX_INDEX_LINES" ]; then
  err "$INDEX" "$index_lines lines, cap is $MAX_INDEX_LINES (rule 6)"
fi

claimed=""
found_doc=0

for doc in "$DIR"/docs/*.md; do
  [ -e "$doc" ] || break
  found_doc=1
  name="${doc##*/}"

  lines=$(wc -l < "$doc")
  if [ "$lines" -gt "$MAX_LINES" ]; then
    err "$doc" "$lines lines, cap is $MAX_LINES - split it (rule 6)"
  fi

  check_whitespace "$doc"

  if [ "$(head -1 "$doc")" != "---" ]; then
    err "$doc:1" "must open with a --- frontmatter block (rule 5)"
  fi

  scope_line=$(sed -n '2,10{/^scope:/p;}' "$doc")
  [ -n "$scope_line" ] || err "$doc" "frontmatter has no scope: (rule 14)"
  [ -n "$(sed -n '2,10{/^verified-at:/p;}' "$doc")" ] ||
    err "$doc" "frontmatter has no verified-at: (rule 13)"

  got_h2=$(grep '^## ' "$doc")
  if [ "$got_h2" != "$want_h2" ]; then
    err "$doc" "## headings must match _TEMPLATE.md exactly and in order (rule 5)"
  fi

  long_fence=$(awk -v max="$MAX_FENCE" '
    /^```/ {
      if (open) { if (NR - start - 1 > max) print start; open = 0 }
      else { open = 1; start = NR }
    }
  ' "$doc" | head -1)
  [ -z "$long_fence" ] ||
    err "$doc:$long_fence" "code fence over $MAX_FENCE lines - cite the file instead (rule 8)"

  lineref=$(grep -nE '\.(go|ts|vue|tmpl|css|md|yml|json):[0-9]+' "$doc" | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  [ -z "$lineref" ] ||
    err "$doc:$lineref" "cites a line number - use the symbol name instead (rule 8)"

  abspath=$(grep -nE '(^|[[:space:]`(])(/home/|/Users/|/root/|[A-Za-z]:\\)' "$doc" |
    head -1 | cut -d: -f1)
  [ -z "$abspath" ] || err "$doc:$abspath" "absolute path - use a repo-relative one (rule 9)"

  grep -q "docs/$name" "$INDEX" || err "$INDEX" "no row pointing at docs/$name (rule 14)"

  while read -r path; do
    [ -n "$path" ] || continue
    [ -e "$path" ] || err "$doc" "scope path does not exist: $path (rule 7)"
    owner=$(printf '%s' "$claimed" | awk -F'|' -v p="$path" '$1 == p { print $2; exit }')
    if [ -n "$owner" ]; then
      err "$doc" "scope path $path is already owned by docs/$owner (rule 2)"
    else
      claimed="${claimed}${path}|${name}
"
    fi
  done < <(printf '%s\n' "${scope_line#scope:}" | tr ',' '\n' |
    sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//')
done

[ "$found_doc" -eq 1 ] || err "$DIR/docs" "contains no docs"

while read -r ref; do
  [ -f "$DIR/$ref" ] || err "$INDEX" "points at $ref, which does not exist (rule 14)"
done < <(grep -oE 'docs/[a-z0-9.-]+\.md' "$INDEX" | sort -u)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- guide/ (rules 16-22)
GUIDE_TEMPLATE="$DIR/guide/_TEMPLATE.md"
MAX_GUIDE_LINES=200
MAX_GUIDE_FENCE=30
guide_count=0

if [ -f "$GUIDE_TEMPLATE" ]; then
  want_guide_h2=$(grep '^## ' "$GUIDE_TEMPLATE")
  check_whitespace "$GUIDE_TEMPLATE"

  for g in "$DIR"/guide/*.md; do
    [ -e "$g" ] || break
    gname="${g##*/}"
    case "$gname" in _TEMPLATE.md) continue ;; esac

    check_whitespace "$g"

    lines=$(wc -l < "$g")
    if [ "$lines" -gt "$MAX_GUIDE_LINES" ]; then
      err "$g" "$lines lines, cap is $MAX_GUIDE_LINES (rule 20)"
    fi

    long_fence=$(awk -v max="$MAX_GUIDE_FENCE" '
      /^```/ {
        if (open) { if (NR - start - 1 > max) print start; open = 0 }
        else { open = 1; start = NR }
      }
    ' "$g" | head -1)
    [ -z "$long_fence" ] ||
      err "$g:$long_fence" "code fence over $MAX_GUIDE_FENCE lines (rule 20)"

    # START-HERE.md has no source doc: exempt from rules 17, 18, 21 (rule 22)
    case "$gname" in START-HERE.md) continue ;; esac

    got_guide_h2=$(grep '^## ' "$g")
    if [ "$got_guide_h2" != "$want_guide_h2" ]; then
      err "$g" "## headings must match guide/_TEMPLATE.md exactly and in order (rule 19)"
    fi

    src=$(sed -n '2,10{/^source:/p;}' "$g" | sed 's/^source: *//')
    stored=$(sed -n '2,10{/^source-hash:/p;}' "$g" | sed 's/^source-hash: *//')
    [ -n "$(sed -n '2,10{/^verified-at:/p;}' "$g")" ] ||
      err "$g" "frontmatter has no verified-at: (rule 16)"
    if [ -z "$src" ] || [ -z "$stored" ]; then
      err "$g" "frontmatter needs source: and source-hash: (rule 16)"
      continue
    fi
    if [ ! -f "$DIR/$src" ]; then
      err "$g" "source: $src does not exist (rule 17)"
      continue
    fi
    if [ "${src##*/}" != "$gname" ]; then
      err "$g" "source: $src must have the same filename as the guide (rule 17)"
    fi

    actual=$(sha256sum "$DIR/$src" | cut -c1-16)
    if [ "$actual" != "$stored" ]; then
      err "$g" "DRIFT: $src changed since this guide was written (hash $stored, now $actual) - regenerate it (rule 18)"
    fi

    # rule 21: a guide may only cite paths its source doc already cites.
    # The doc's citations are its backticked tokens plus its scope: paths; trailing
    # slashes are normalised, and citing a directory whose files the doc cites is allowed.
    src_paths=$({ grep -oE '`[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+`' "$DIR/$src" | tr -d '`'
                  sed -n '2,10{/^scope:/p;}' "$DIR/$src" | sed 's/^scope: *//' | tr ',' '\n'
                } | sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*$//; s|/*$||' | sort -u)
    while read -r path; do
      [ -n "$path" ] || continue
      printf '%s\n' "$src_paths" | grep -qxF "$path" && continue
      printf '%s\n' "$src_paths" | grep -qE "^${path//./\\.}/" && continue
      err "$g" "cites $path, which $src does not - the guide adds explanation, not facts (rule 21)"
    done < <(grep -oE '`[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+`' "$g" | tr -d '`' | sed 's|/*$||' | sort -u |
      while read -r c; do
        case "$c" in */*) [ -e "$c" ] && printf '%s\n' "$c" ;; esac
      done)

    guide_count=$((guide_count + 1))
  done
fi

if [ "$fail" -eq 0 ]; then
  ndocs=$(find "$DIR/docs" -name '*.md' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
  printf 'check.sh: ok (%s docs, guide %s/%s)\n' "$ndocs" "$guide_count" "$ndocs"
fi
exit "$fail"

# AI Logs

This folder holds every AI session for each sprint, one folder per student. The course rules are on
the [AI Log Instructions](https://csci-435-se.github.io/ai-logs/) page and the current sprint page
at <https://csci-435-se.github.io/>. This README is the team's shared convention for following them.

## What to log

Every AI session tied to this project: code, debugging, tests, reviews, drafting issues and PRs,
design discussion, the sprint report. That includes sessions that went nowhere. Purely academic
questions unrelated to the project don't need logging.

## Structure

```
ai-logs/
  sprint1/
    <github-username>/                          ← exact GitHub username, matching case
      .gitkeep                                  ← the folder must exist even if you used no AI
      YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md
      YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>/           ← attachments (images, etc.), optional
```

Team folders: `ab-wm`, `arjunsb26`, `CarsonRackley`, `controlled-opposition`, `Jack-Donohue`,
`vvchopra`.

## Naming

`YYYY-MM-DD_<tool>_<short-slug>.md`

- **Date:** the day the session started.
- **Sprint folder:** the sprint that date falls in, not the sprint the work is for.
- **Tool:** one of the course identifiers: `claude-code`, `claude-web`, `claude-desktop`, `cursor`,
  `gemini-cli`, `codex-cli`, `copilot`, `chatgpt`, `other-<name>`. Claude Code run inside VS Code is
  `claude-code`.
- **Slug:** lowercase words joined with hyphens that say what the session did. Put the issue number
  first when there is one: `issue-52-impl`, `issue-52-spec`, `pr-61-review`, `sprint1-report`.
  Replace auto-generated slugs such as `local-command-caveat...`.
- **Formats:** `.md` is preferred; `.txt` and `.json` are also accepted. No `.docx`, `.pdf`, `.html`
  or share links.

## Capturing a session

| Tool | How |
| --- | --- |
| Claude Code (terminal or VS Code), other agentic CLIs | Start it with [SpecStory](https://specstory.com/): `specstory run claude`, from the repo root. Forgot? Run `specstory sync` afterwards; it back-fills from Claude Code's local history. Then copy from `.specstory/history/` (git-ignored) into your folder and rename it to the convention. |
| Web chat (claude.ai, ChatGPT, Gemini, ...) | Install a browser chat exporter and export the session as Markdown right after it ends. Include any files you pasted in as context. |
| Claude Desktop | SpecStory doesn't capture it. Copy the conversation into a `.md` file by hand. |

At the end of each sprint, run `specstory sync` once more and re-copy. A log copied mid-session is
incomplete.

## Content

- The **tool and AI model** used (SpecStory writes both).
- The **complete** prompt and response history. For agentic tools, that includes file edits and
  commands (SpecStory includes them). Logs with missing responses or truncated histories are
  **invalid**. Don't hand-write, summarise or trim a log; only rename it.
- Attachments (screenshots, snippets) go in a folder with the log's name minus `.md`.
- Log **every** session, including ones that went nowhere. Grading is on how complete the record
  is, not on whether AI helped.

## Where logs are referenced

- **Issue comments only.** Each contributor posts their own `### AI Assistance — @username` comment
  on the issue, with full `https://github.com/...` links to their logs. Format:
  [`.claude-students/AI-ASSISTANCE.md`](../.claude-students/AI-ASSISTANCE.md).
- **Not** in PR descriptions or PR comments. The PR has a short AI-use note with no log link. The
  AI Log Instructions page says "Issue/PR comments", but the Sprint 1 page narrows this to issue
  comments only, and the sprint page wins.
- Each teammate posts their own comment, including reviewers who used AI to review.
- No AI used? Post an issue comment saying so, and keep your folder with its `.gitkeep`.
- The sprint report lists each member's tools, session count, folder link, and 2–3 sentences on
  lessons learned.

checkin
diagrams
report.md
screenshots

442-
443:### Flaky test<a href="#flaky-test" class="headerlink" title="Permanent link">¶</a>
444-
445-A test that sometimes passes and sometimes fails on the same code,
446-without any change. Common causes: timing and waits, test order, shared
447-state between tests, time zones and dates, and database results returned
448:in an unstable order. A flaky test is a problem even when it usually
449-passes: people stop trusting red CI runs. Fix the cause rather than
450-retrying or skipping the test; if you must skip it, link an issue and
451-give the reason in a code comment.
452-
453:### Hardening issue<a href="#hardening-issue" class="headerlink"
454-title="Permanent link">¶</a>
455-
456-An issue that makes the existing system more reliable instead of adding
457:a feature: fixing a bug, a flaky test, a failing or missing CI check, or
458:tests that fail on `main`. Hardening issues are scoped like any other
459-issue and must include evidence that the problem is fixed (see the
460-[Sprint 3](../sprint3/) page).
461-
462-### Linter / formatter<a href="#linter-formatter" class="headerlink"
463-title="Permanent link">¶</a>
464-
--
492-A way to measure test quality. The tool makes small deliberate changes
493:("mutants") to the code, such as flipping `>` to `>=`, and reruns the
494:tests. If the tests still pass, the mutant "survived," meaning the tests
495-would not notice that bug. Example tools for mutation testing: StrykerJS
496-(JavaScript/TypeScript), Gremlins (Go).
497-
498:### Mutant (killed / survived / no coverage)<a href="#mutant-killed-survived-no-coverage" class="headerlink"
499-title="Permanent link">¶</a>
500-
501-A copy of the code with one small change made by a mutation testing
502-tool, for example `a > b` changed to `a >= b`, or a function call
503:removed. Each mutant ends with a status:
504-
505-- **Killed:** at least one test failed, so the tests noticed the change.
506-  This is what you want.
507-- **Survived:** all tests passed. Either your tests have a gap, or the
508:  mutant is equivalent (see below).
509-- **No coverage:** no test executes the changed line at all.
510-- **Timeout:** the change made the code run too long (e.g., an infinite
511-  loop); usually counted as killed.
512-
513:### Equivalent mutant<a href="#equivalent-mutant" class="headerlink"
514-title="Permanent link">¶</a>
515-
516:A mutant that behaves exactly like the original code, so no test can
517-ever kill it. Example: changing `i < n` to `i != n` in a loop where `i`
518-starts at 0, increases by 1, and `n` is never negative. Equivalent
519:mutants are not test gaps; when you report one, explain why the behavior
520-is the same.
521-
522-### Mutation score<a href="#mutation-score" class="headerlink"
523-title="Permanent link">¶</a>
524-
525:The percentage of mutants that were killed (killed ÷ all mutants,
526-usually excluding equivalent ones). A higher score means the tests catch
527-more of the injected changes. The score is only meaningful for the files
528-that were mutated, and a high score does not prove the tests check the
529-right behavior.
530-

552-PR requires writing or updating tests for any code changed. "CI green"
553-means the test suite (and other checks) pass on GitHub after your push.

185:**Why not forks?** Forking is the standard model for contributing to open-source projects where you *don't* have write access: you fork to your own GitHub account, clone your fork, and open a PR from your fork back to the original. You will encounter this when contributing to the upstream project. But for your course team — where everyone has write access to the shared repo — it just adds confusion: two clones on your machine, two remotes to keep in sync, merge conflicts that are harder to reason about.

The user found its default output "insufferable": long walkthroughs, an 80% docstring-coverage check, and "Summary by CodeRabbit" written into every graded PR description. On 2026-10-07 Claude drafted `.coderabbit.yaml` on branch `chore/abhoot-ai-log-sprint-1`. The first draft was too thin ("a bit light"). The user wants it to enforce the course requirements and Gitea's CONTRIBUTING.md, within reason: role-play as if PRs go upstream, but course rules win, and this is not a business setting. Each instruction should cite a written rule. Noise stays low: four warning-only checks (course PR description, screenshots, tests, breaking/dependency) and per-path instructions.

Schema facts checked against https://coderabbit.ai/integrations/schema.v2.json on 2026-10-07:
- The "Security Architecture Review", "Merge Risk" and "Architecture Summary" blocks have no config key. Only `tone_instructions` can steer them.
- `profile` accepts `quiet`, `chill` or `assertive`.
- `tone_instructions` has a 250-character limit.
- Check modes must be quoted as `"off"`, because an unquoted `off` parses as a boolean.

**How to apply:** keep later changes small. Validate with yamllint, plus jsonschema via `uv run --no-project --with jsonschema --with pyyaml`. Related: [[never-commit-or-submit]], [[temp-files-in-specstory]].
----
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://coderabbit.ai/integrations/schema.v2.json
# CodeRabbit settings for the CSCI 435 fork; every key is in https://docs.coderabbit.ai/reference/configuration
# Reviews treat each PR as if it were going upstream to go-gitea/gitea; where the course rules differ, they win.
language: en-US
tone_instructions: "Review like a Gitea maintainer helping a student team with little time. Raise real bugs, security holes, unmet acceptance criteria and broken repo rules. Start each comment with Required or Optional. Be brief: no praise or style nits."

reviews:
  profile: chill
  high_level_summary: false # PR descriptions are graded, so the bot must not write into them
  sequence_diagrams: false
  estimate_code_review_effort: false
  related_issues: false
  related_prs: false
  suggested_labels: false
  suggested_reviewers: false
  in_progress_fortune: false
  enable_prompt_for_ai_agents: false
  auto_review:
    auto_incremental_review: false # one review when the PR leaves draft; comment "@coderabbitai review" for another
  path_filters:
    - "!ai-logs/**" # course logs are filed unedited
    - "!.claude-students/guide/**" # generated from .claude-students/docs
    - "!docs/superpowers/**" # AI planning notes
    - "!templates/swagger/v1_json.tmpl" # generated, and CI checks it is up to date
    - "!templates/swagger/v1_openapi3_json.tmpl"
    - "!web_src/fomantic/build/**" # vendored
  path_instructions:
    - path: "**"
      instructions: |
        The project rules are AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/sprint0/standards.md, docs/guidelines-backend.md, docs/guidelines-frontend.md, and the .claude-students/docs page that .claude-students/INDEX.md maps to the changed path. Cite the rule when you raise one.
        Course rules win where they differ from upstream: PRs here are merged with a merge commit, and AI logs and .claude-students docs are committed on purpose.
        - Scope: a PR covers one issue. Flag changes unrelated to the linked issue (CONTRIBUTING.md: "Don't make changes unrelated to your PR").
        - Layers: imports flow cmd → routers → services → models → modules only. Flag an import against that direction.
        - Comments: short, explaining why, never narrating the code. Flag a removed comment that is still true. Never ask for docstrings.
        - Docs drift: if the change makes a statement in a .claude-students/docs page wrong, ask for that page to be fixed in the same PR (AGENTS.md).
        - Commits: a commit made with AI help, including one pushed by a bot, ends with an `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` trailer, and no commit carries `Co-Authored-By` or `Signed-off-by` (AGENTS.md, .claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md). If possible, the message also names the person who approved the change, since a human approves every commit.
        - Skip anything `make fmt`, `make lint-go`, `make lint-js`, `make lint-css` or `make lint-templates` enforces; CI runs them.
    - path: "**/*.go"
      instructions: |
        - A new .go file starts with `// Copyright <current year> The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.` and `// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT`.
        - Writes that must roll back together run inside `db.WithTx` or `db.WithTx2`, and every function in the transaction takes `context.Context` first.
        - XORM: flag an `Update` or `Delete` with no `Where` or ID condition; it touches every row.
        - Before reading or changing another user's or repository's data, the doer's permission is checked. Treat a missing check as a security bug.
        - Handlers fail through the context helpers (`ctx.NotFound`, `ctx.ServerError`, `ctx.JSONError` and the like), never by writing the response by hand.
        - User-visible text is a locale key, never a literal; user-facing errors go through `util.ErrorWrapTranslatable`.
        - `go.mod` and `go.sum` change only when the feature needs it, after `make tidy`.
    - path: "**/*_test.go"
      instructions: |
        - Prefer a unit test next to the code over an integration test when the logic can be tested alone (AGENTS.md).
        - A new test package has `func TestMain(m *testing.M) { unittest.MainTest(m) }`, or its fixtures never load.
        - Cover the normal case, invalid input and permission checks where they apply (docs/sprint0/standards.md).
        - Integration tests should run in under 2 seconds. Don't ask for tests beyond what the acceptance criteria need.
    - path: "models/migrations/**"
      instructions: |
        - A new migration is appended at the bottom of the slice in `migrations.go`. Never insert in the middle, renumber, or edit a migration that is already on main.
        - It lives in `v1_27/v<id>.go` and declares its own local copy of each struct inside the function. It never imports a live model from `models/`.
        - Partial table changes use `SyncWithOptions` with `IgnoreDropIndices` and `IgnoreConstrains`, not plain `Sync`.
        - A column added to an existing table is `NOT NULL DEFAULT <value>`, so old rows are filled.
        - It has a `v<id>_test.go`, whose fixtures folder under `models/migrations/fixtures/` matches the test function name exactly.
    - path: "routers/api/v1/**"
      instructions: |
        - Never break v1: no removed or renamed fields, changed field types, changed status codes or removed endpoints (docs/guidelines-backend.md).
        - Every result, success and each error, is documented in the route's swagger comment. Request and response bodies are structs in `modules/structs/`, registered under `routers/api/v1/swagger/`.
        - Status codes: GET 200, POST 201 with the created object, PUT 204, PATCH 200 with the changed object, DELETE 204.
        - Edit endpoints take every field as optional except the ones that identify the object. List endpoints accept `page` and `limit` and set `X-Total-Count` via `ctx.SetTotalCountHeader`.
        - Where GitHub's API has the same concept, use its endpoint and field names.
    - path: "modules/structs/**"
      instructions: |
        These structs are the public API. Flag a removed or renamed field, or a changed JSON name or type, as breaking v1.
    - path: "templates/**"
      instructions: |
        - Every user-visible string goes through `ctx.Locale.Tr`, or `ctx.Locale.TrN` for plurals, and its key exists in `locale_en-US.json`.
        - Hide and show with the `tw-hidden` class. Use `tw-` utilities and `flex-*` helpers rather than per-child margins (AGENTS.md).
        - Ids and classes are kebab-case with 2–3 feature keywords. Use `<button>` and other semantic elements rather than a clickable `<div>`.
        - User content reaches the page through the existing render and sanitiser helpers. Flag user input inserted as raw HTML as a security bug (.claude-students/docs/modules-markup.md).
    - path: "web_src/js/**"
      instructions: |
        Follow docs/guidelines-frontend.md:
        - Use `import type` for type-only imports and `@ts-expect-error`, not `@ts-ignore`.
        - Use `!` rather than `?.` or `??` when a value always exists (AGENTS.md).
        - Mark a function `async` only when it awaits or returns a Promise. An async event listener calls `e.preventDefault()` before its first `await`.
        - Requests use the `GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` wrappers from `modules/fetch.ts`. Read data attributes with `getAttribute`, not `dataset`, and never bind user-provided data directly onto DOM nodes.
        - Show and hide with `showElem`, `hideElem` and `toggleElem`; prefix custom DOM events with `ce-`.
        - Don't mix Vue with Fomantic-UI, and don't use JSX.
        - No user-visible literals: text comes from a locale key, through `data-locale-*` attributes or `window.config.i18n`.
        - New logic in a `.ts` module gets a vitest `*.test.ts` file next to it.
    - path: "web_src/css/**"
      instructions: |
        - Prefer `tw-` utilities and `flex-*` helpers; use `gt-` or `g-` helpers only when no Tailwind utility exists.
        - Avoid `!important`. Where it can't be avoided, a comment says why.
        - Add a new, prefixed class rather than restyling a Fomantic class.
        - Colours come from the theme's `var(--color-*)` variables, never a literal colour, or the other themes break (.claude-students/docs/frontend-css.md).
    - path: "docs/sprint2/diagrams/**"
      instructions: |
        Course deliverable D6 (.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md, "UML diagrams (D6)"); review it as a course submission, not as code.
        - Files are named `<issue#>-<github-username>-class.png`, `<issue#>-<github-username>-sequence.png` (or `.pdf`) and `<issue#>-<github-username>.md`.
        - The `.md` embeds both diagrams under "## Class Diagram" and "## Sequence Diagram", and answers every question under "## Q&A": 3 class-diagram, 3 sequence-diagram and 1 AI-use question ("N/A" is valid for AI use).
        - Flag class or method names in the diagram or answers that do not exist in the code or in the linked PR.
        - Flag a missing note on how Go structs, interfaces and embedding map to UML.
    - path: "docs/sprint2/checkin/**"
      instructions: |
        Course deliverable D7: `docs/sprint2/checkin/<github-username>.md`, due Oct 22. It answers three questions in about 150 words each: what is done and what remains, one thing learned, one thing to do differently. Flag a missing answer or one only a sentence or two long. Do not comment on writing style.
    - path: "options/locale/**"
      instructions: |
        - Only `locale_en-US.json` is edited by hand. Edits to any other locale file are overwritten by the Crowdin sync and must be reverted (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Translation").
        - A new key sits next to its neighbours in the same area. A plural is a `_1` and `_n` pair, both using `%d`.
        - Flag a new key that nothing uses, and a removed key that something still uses.
  finishing_touches: # a human approves every commit (AGENTS.md), so the bot never pushes code; its commits also lack the Assisted-by trailer the course requires
    docstrings:
      enabled: false
    unit_tests:
      enabled: false
    autofix:
      enabled: false
    fix_ci:
      enabled: false
    resolve_merge_conflict:
      enabled: false
  pre_merge_checks:
    docstrings:
      mode: "off" # AGENTS.md wants short "why" comments, not a docstring on every function
    title:
      mode: "off" # the pr-title CI job already checks Conventional Commits
    description:
      mode: "off" # replaced by the course-specific check below
    issue_assessment:
      mode: warning
    custom_checks:
      - name: Course PR description
        mode: warning
        instructions: |
          Judge only the PR description. Pass only if all of these hold, otherwise fail and list what is missing:
          - Each issue the PR closes is on its own line, as "Closes #<number>", "Fixes #<number>" or "Resolves #<number>".
          - It has these sections, each with the author's own text rather than only the template's comments: "What changed", "Why", "How it was tested", "CI / manual verification", "Design", "Tech Debt", "AI assistance".
          - When the linked issue lists acceptance criteria, "Why" names the ones the PR satisfies (AC1, AC2, ...).
          - "Tech Debt" has an "Introduced:" line and an "Encountered:" line, each with the author's own text or "None.". Missing this section costs grading points (Sprint 2, D4).
          - When "Design" states a design decision rather than pointing at the issue's, it names at least two alternatives (Sprint 2, D3).
          - "AI assistance" either says "No AI used", or names the tool and model, what the AI did, and what the author did to check it.
          - Nothing links to a file under ai-logs/. AI logs belong in the issue's AI Assistance comment (.claude-students/AI-ASSISTANCE.md).
      - name: Screenshots for UI changes
        mode: warning

          Pass if no file under templates/ or web_src/css/, and no .vue file, changed.
          Otherwise pass only if the PR description contains at least one image (Markdown image syntax or an <img> tag), and fail asking for after screenshots, plus before screenshots for a fix (CONTRIBUTING.md, "PR title and summary").
      - name: Tests for behaviour changes
        mode: warning
        instructions: |
          Pass if no non-test file under cmd/, models/, modules/, routers/, services/ or web_src/js/ changed.

      - name: Breaking and dependency changes

The description needs a reason and a "BREAKING" section saying how users are affected and how to adapt (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Breaking PRs").
          - go.mod, go.sum, package.json or pnpm-lock.yaml changed. The description says why the dependency change is needed (docs/guidelines-backend.md, "Dependencies").

knowledge_base:

----
- Read `.claude-students/INDEX.md` before exploring the tree: it maps each subpackage to a short context doc, so read the 1-3 docs matching your task instead. Fix any doc you find wrong in the same PR; editing a `docs/*.md` also requires regenerating its `guide/*.md` twin. Run `./.claude-students/check.sh` before pushing. See `.claude-students/README.md` and `MAINTENANCE.md`
- Use `make help` to find available development targets
- Run `make fmt` to format `.go` files, and run `make lint-go` to lint them
- Run `make lint-js` to lint `.ts` files
- Run `make tidy` after any `go.mod` changes
- Run single go tests with `go test -run '^TestName$' ./modulepath/`
- Run single js test files with `pnpm exec vitest <path-filter>`
- Run single playwright e2e test files with `GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='<filepath>' make test-e2e`
- Add the current year into the copyright header of new `.go` files
- Ensure no trailing whitespace in edited files
- Use Conventional Commits for commit messages and PR titles, e.g. `type(scope): subject`, ending commit subjects with the issue number, e.g. `(#17)`; `!` before the colon if breaking. Use `test` type for test-only changes.
- Never force-push, amend, or squash unless asked. Use new commits and normal push for pull request updates
71:## Testing expectations
72-
73-- Every code change must add or update tests. Prefer unit tests when the logic can be tested on its own
74-  (`AGENTS.md`).
75-- Go unit tests go next to the code in `*_test.go` files, named `TestXxx`. Run a single test with
76-  `go test -run '^TestName$' ./modulepath/`.
77-- Tests for routes and pages go in `tests/integration/`.
78-- Frontend tests go next to the file as `*.test.ts`. Run them with `pnpm exec vitest <path>`.
79-- End-to-end tests use Playwright: `GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='<filepath>' make test-e2e`.
80-- Test the normal case, invalid input, and permission checks where they apply, and try UI changes in a
81-  local instance.
82-- Run tests in WSL or Linux. Native Windows produces errors that are not related to your change.
83-- Some tests may already fail on main. Run the same test on main before assuming your change broke it.
84-- See `docs/testing.md` for more details.
85-- Run tests on localhost to validate the fix does what you want and you get the expected results in the
86-  dev environment.
87-
88-## AI tool use
89-
90-Given the nature of the course, the use of AI is permitted, if not encouraged. It goes without saying
91-that using AI comes with the following caveats:
92-
